doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Florian Ross's live record
summary: Liebman recalls a live date with the young German pianist-composer Florian Ross, whom Kirchner thinks underrated.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Here’s a record I’m fond of, by somebody I’m fond of. That’s Florian Ross’s record.
One of the great undersung musicians of our time, I think.

This is when he was very young. He is a great musician. That was, I remember, live. We did that live. The first night was completely out. Second night was perfect. I came off the plane first night. I was out of tune. I was screwed up. We had a long conference the next day. I said, do a couple of changes, couple of this, couple of that, and that record is a very nice record. I haven’t heard it in years, but his writing – he’s a heavy cat.
Yeah. He sends me all his stuff.
I’ve seen him. He’s still writing. He’s got three kids or something like that.
Yeah. He’s got three kids, but he’s done – he did a record with a brass section, and he did a record with five saxes and rhythm. He’s done a couple things.
He’s done a couple quintet records, a couple trio records, a solo record.
I was very impressed with him.
I think he’s one of the heaviest young – heaviest musicians under 50.
He’s got to be in his mid-30s by now.
He was born in ’72. So he’s 38. I tell people about him. Nobody knows him.
They don’t even know him in Europe.
